items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 28:1
items.html: At the time of the coupling in the upper phase, the reflected light that descends from there into the empty vessel is found to prevail over the record that is there. And although the record is much greater than the descending reflected light, nevertheless, since the record is from after the departure of its coupling while the descending reflected light is drawn from the illumination of the coupling, it therefore prevails over it. And afterwards, when the screen has been refined from the upper phase as well and the coupling has departed there too, the record returns and prevails over the descending reflected light — that is, over the sparks that fell into its vessel — and the record descends again to its vessel as at first and nullifies their force, until they return and are renewed afterwards in the second expansion. (Chapter 3, Inner Light, Item 80, and Chapter 4, Inner Light, Item 7)
